title: Streaming Throttle Orchestrator: kernel-aware flow control and tail-latency attenuation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Persistent single-request and microburst tail spikes remain in high-concurrency streaming workloads. Root causes identified in telemetry include mismatched kernel paths (small vs large attention kernels), late prefill/kv-cache warms, and uncoordinated decode admission that forces small low-priority requests into long-running GPU kernels causing head-of-line blocking.

Goal: Implement a Streaming Throttle Orchestrator (STO) in the serving runtime to harmonize admission, kernel selection hints, and decode pacing for streaming/prefill flows to reduce 95th/99th latency while preserving throughput and packability. STO should be pluggable per-tenant and respect SLO tiers (hosted vs dedicated).

High-level design:
- Admission layer: lightweight per-GPU flow controller that maintains soft tokens per kernel-family and per-tenant. Tokens are returned after prefill completion or after decode handoff. The controller supports fast-path admit for short-prefill requests and progressive admission for long-prefill decodes.
- Kernel hints: on admit, STO emits a kernel preference hint (attn_small/attn_large/quantized_fast) based on sequence-length histogram and attention sparsity estimate from the first N tokens. Hints are advisory to the kernel selector and used to avoid expensive kernel-switching mid-batch.
- Decode pacing & handoff: integrate a pacing step that delays low-priority streaming decodes by up to configurable X ms to allow packing into an upcoming batch, with guarantees: max stall = 30ms for P2/P3 tenants, and 0ms for P0. Handoff respects KV-cache readiness signals and will escalate to immediate decode if stall budget exhausted.
- Graceful fallback: when GPU kernel capacity for a family is saturated, STO can reroute admits to compatible quantized kernel variants or enqueue in a secondary 'pack-and-drain' queue to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- Observability: add per-tenant, per-kernel-family time series: admit_latency, kernel_switch_count, delayed_decode_ms, and tail-CDFs (50/90/95/99). Include a debug trace that links request IDs to kernel hint and actual kernel chosen.
acceptance_criteria:
1) 95th token latency reduced by >=25% on internal SLO test harness for mixed short/long streaming workload compared to baseline runtime-1.20.
2) Kernel-switch incidents (mid-batch kernel change) reduced to <1% of batches.
3) No throughput regression >5% on peak load.
4) New metrics ingested into Console dashboards and a canary test showing per-tenant admit and delay breakdowns.
5) Feature flag gated rollout with canary (10% traffic) and automatic rollback on error rate increase >2x.
comments: 2026-02-23 — Initial scoping meeting: agreed to target both admit and kernel-hint surfaces. Action: Marco to prototype token accounting; Aisha to draft design doc.

2026-02-27 — Prototype results: token accounting + small hint reduced kernel switches in batch-playback by ~40% in lab. Observed 12ms median added admit overhead; acceptable. Action: instrument decode pacing timers and tie into KV-cache ready signal.

2026-03-03 — Design review feedback from Runtime team: prefer advisory hints to hard overrides to avoid breaking kernel selector heuristics. Added fallback path to quantized variant. Action: update design doc and prepare RFC PR.

2026-03-05 — RFC created: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Streaming+Throttle+Orchestrator and draft implementation here: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2841. Requesting reviews from @emily.chen and @raj.khan.

2026-03-08 — Integration test: canary harness simulating 80/20 short/long tokens gave 28% reduction at p95 after enabling 25ms decode pacing for P2 tenants. Noted slight increase in p50 for short requests when pacing is on; trade-off documented.

2026-03-10 — QA: added tests for kernel-hint stability under synthetic jitter and for starvation scenarios when stall budget is repeatedly exhausted. Next: rollout to staging canary (5% traffic) and monitor metrics for 48h.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: decode pacing may increase median latency for very short requests. Mitigation: tiered stall budget and per-tenant opt-out plus telemetry-based automatic disable for affected endpoints.
Risk: kernel hints could be ignored by kernel selector causing wasted work. Mitigation: make hints advisory and add kernel-switch budget metric to detect and back off.
Risk: admission token accounting bug could cause live traffic drops. Mitigation: start with read-only instrumentation, then canary small traffic, add circuit-breaker to bypass STO on error.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag build into runtime, internal dev cluster smoke tests. 2) Staging canary (5% traffic) for 48h with alerting on p95/p99 and error rate. 3) Gradual ramp to 25% then 50% with metrics audit. 4) Dedicated customers opt-in for alpha (manual). 5) Full rollout after 2 successful waves and sign-off from SRE and PM.
notes: This ticket focuses on serving-layer coordination and does not change public API. Follow-up ticket will add console UX for per-tenant stall budgets and an auto-tune recommendation engine. Consider later integration with Optimize for automatic stall budget recommendations.
